data.title: Gene Munster Says Apple’s $2,200 iPhone Duo Could Add $8B To FY27 Revenue, Sees 20M Units In Sales Even As Wall Street Expects Only 12M
data.description:
Key points:
  • Munster said his initial observations from Apple stores on launch morning strengthened his conviction in his 20 million-unit forecast, which would represent roughly 7% of total iPhone unit sales in FY27.
  • He pointed to shorter launch-day lines compared with the iPhone XS and XS Max launch in 2018, but argued that the comparison needs to account for the iPhone Duo’s much higher price.
  • Munster views the combination of fewer buyers and significantly higher revenue per device as evidence of a solid start rather than a weak one.

Apple Inc.’s (AAPL) $2,200 iPhone Duo appears to be getting off to a stronger start than Wall Street anticipated, with long lines at Apple stores on launch day prompting longtime Apple watcher Gene Munster to raise his confidence in the device’s sales prospects.

Munster, managing partner at Deepwater Asset Management, expects Apple to sell 20 million iPhone Duo units in fiscal 2027, well above Wall Street’s roughly 12 million-unit estimate. He said the higher-priced device could become a meaningful contributor to Apple’s overall iPhone growth.

Apple shares ended with a decline of 0.1% in Friday’s regular trade, edged lower by 0.03% in the afterhours session.

Munster Sees 20M iPhone Duo Sales

Munster said his initial observations from Apple stores on launch morning strengthened his conviction in his 20 million-unit forecast, which would represent roughly 7% of total iPhone unit sales in FY27.

The forecast compares with the Street’s expectation of around 12 million units. Munster noted that the difference of roughly eight million incremental units could add about 3% to overall iPhone growth in FY27.

The bigger factor, however, is the iPhone Duo’s significantly higher selling price. Munster estimates that the additional customers would be moving from an iPhone with an average selling price of about $1,200 to the $2,200 Duo.

That combination could add approximately $8 billion to the Street’s current FY27 iPhone revenue estimate of $279 billion, according to Munster.

High Price Could Make iPhone Duo A Revenue Driver, Says Munster

Munster’s bullishness comes despite the Duo’s relatively higher price compared to other iPhones. The investor pointed to shorter launch-day lines compared with the iPhone XS and XS Max launch in 2018, but argued that the comparison needs to account for the Duo’s much higher price.

He noted that the iPhone Duo’s price is about 82% higher than the iPhone XS Max was at launch. As a result, Munster views the combination of fewer buyers and significantly higher revenue per device as evidence of a solid start rather than a weak one.

Wall Street currently expects the Duo to remain a niche product, accounting for about 4% of iPhone units and 7% of iPhone revenue in FY27. Munster is considerably more bullish, projecting the device will represent 8% of units and 16% of revenue.

He expects Apple’s overall iPhone business to grow 13% in FY27, compared with the Street’s 10% forecast, with the Duo providing part of that lift. Looking further ahead, he sees the device contributing even more meaningfully to the iPhone lineup in FY28.

What Wall Street Thinks

Last week, analysts at Evercore ISI noted that iPhone Duo delivery dates quickly stretched to late January across tracked regions and configurations, calling the demand signal “solidly out of the gate” while cautioning that supply constraints could also be contributing.

Munster similarly said lead times stabilizing around Jan. 25 increased his confidence in a 20 million-unit FY27 forecast, though he acknowledged Apple’s production capacity remains unknown.

The investor also noted that iPhone 18 Pro lead times have cooled, while Pro Max demand has held up better.

What Retail Traders Think Of AAPL Stock

Retail sentiment on Stocktwits around Apple trended in the ‘bearish’ territory at the time of writing.

AAPL stock is up 28% year-to-date and 34% over the past 12 months. The S&P 500 ETF Trust (SPY) is up 11% over the past 12 months, while the Invesco QQQ Trust (QQQ) is up 15%.

data.title: France's luxury stores board up windows ahead of fresh protests
data.description:
Key points:
  • Rolex, De Beers among Parisian stores closed on day of protests
  • Luxury stores add security staffing, board up windows
  • Industry already grappling with slowing demand

By Alessandro Parodi

Luxury boutiques in France boarded up their normally glitzy shopfronts and hired private security ahead of fresh protests on Saturday, with some planning to stay closed after rioters looted stores across the country last weekend.

France, the world's most visited country, attracts large numbers of overseas shoppers seeking Chanel handbags and Hermes scarves, an important source of revenue for luxury brands grappling with slowing demand.

But some decided staying open was too risky after last week's unrest, when rioters smashed and looted hundreds of shops in Paris, Marseille and Bordeaux.

A Rolex retailer and a De Beers store near Paris' Place Vendome will remain closed on Saturday, staff said, while managers at stores including Richemont-owned IWC said they would decide whether to close early depending on the scale of the protests.

Signs on the heavily boarded-up windows of Adidas and Boss stores on the Champs Elysees informed customers they would be closed, while employees at Swatch Group stores said they would shut early.

A Lacoste store was entirely covered by metal cages after suffering what a staff member described as "enormous" damage last week. A café owned by the brand was completely boarded up.

Groups including France's main student union, UNEF, and the Yellow Vest movement, which emerged as a powerful anti-establishment force in 2018, plan to march through central Paris later on Saturday to protest against high living costs and cuts to public services.

Near the Arc de Triomphe, tourists photographed boarded-up stores and restaurants as they tried to take selfies beneath the landmark before the protests begin.

Hotel staff said they were advising worried guests on the protest route and areas to avoid, leaving major tourist streets largely empty despite a heavy police and private security presence.

NOT IN THE MOOD

Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez said on Friday that 70,000 police officers, backed by specialist units, would be deployed to prevent a repeat of last week's violence.

But staff at LVMH brands Louis Vuitton, Dior and Bulgari said they were taking no chances and security at their stores near Place Vendome had been increased. The group had also deployed additional private security to patrol high-end shopping districts, several employees said.

Nearby department store Printemps has also increased its security staff, carried out repairs and reinforced shop windows and entrances, a spokesperson said.

Hermes finance chief Eric du Halgouet said this week the company had strengthened security at its French stores, adding it was too early to assess the impact of recent events on business.

The image-conscious industry can ill afford further negative publicity. Consumer sentiment is gloomy worldwide and tourism is slowing as a result of the Iran war, contributing to disappointing quarterly results this month from LVMH , Hermes and Kering .

Lidiya Shevchenko, a sales assistant at a Graziella Braccialini store, said she doubted many people would be looking to visit stores anyway during the protests.

"I suppose the mood is just as important when it comes to shopping," Shevchenko said.

One tourist already thinking twice is Cambodian Jerry Lay, who purchased several items from Louis Vuitton on the Champs-Élysées earlier this week.

"We do enjoy shopping in France, but after experiencing the protest (last Saturday), I'd say it's 50/50 whether I would consider coming back next time," Lay said.

data.title: BTCC Reports $387 Billion In Futures Trading As TradFi-Linked Contracts Grow
data.description:
TL;DR: Crypto exchange BTCC says quarterly futures volume reached $387 billion and its TradFi-linked trading category increased to $16.3 billion, based on company-reported data.

Crypto exchange BTCC says demand for its futures products accelerated during the third quarter, including a sharp increase in contracts linked to traditional financial markets.

The company reported $387 billion in futures trading volume for Q3 2026 in figures released Thursday. It also put trading in its so-called TradFi category at $16.3 billion, up from approximately $2.7 billion in the previous quarter. Both figures come from the exchange's own growth report and should be read as self-reported metrics rather than an independent market-share audit.

Why exchanges are looking beyond crypto pairs

Digital-asset trading platforms have increasingly experimented with derivatives that reference equity indices, stocks, commodities and other familiar market exposures. A trader already using an exchange for Bitcoin perpetual contracts may be attracted by the prospect of managing additional positions through the same interface.

The economic difference lies in what is being traded. A derivative tied to a stock or fund does not confer the same rights as owning the underlying security. Counterparty exposure, contract funding and margin requirements can introduce risks that are unrelated to the performance of the named company.

BTCC frames its growth partly around lower trading barriers and new product categories. Lower minimums may broaden access, but they can also make it easier for inexperienced participants to take on leveraged exposure without appreciating liquidation mechanics.

Volume numbers need context

Large headline volumes are common in derivatives because the notional value of contracts traded can far exceed money actually deposited as margin. Heavy turnover therefore does not imply that hundreds of billions of fresh cash entered the exchange during the quarter.

The report also highlights rising registered-account numbers and what BTCC describes as a healthy reserve ratio. Such disclosures are useful starting points, but reserve claims are strongest when backed by independently reviewable liabilities and asset records, not only a promotional percentage.

Comparisons between exchanges are difficult when methodologies for counting derivatives volume, active users and internal market-making activity differ. Traders should pay at least as much attention to spreads, depth, risk controls and withdrawal arrangements as they do to a quarterly volume figure.

The growth report suggests that crypto-native venues see an opportunity in offering broader market exposure. Whether that opportunity becomes lasting revenue will depend on customer retention, regulatory availability and the quality of those products when conditions turn volatile.

Source: www.globenewswire.com original announcement or data.

Related Reading: crypto exchanges; Bitcoin; tokenized assets.

Written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

data.title: You Are Inheriting a Portfolio of Unwanted Investments. How to Fix It. — Barrons.com
data.description:
By Mallika Mitr a

Financial advisor Katrina Soelter recently worked with a client who had received a seven-figure inheritance that included unwanted shares of oil companies and of Palantir. The software company has been at the center of several controversies, most recently revolving around links to surveillance and deportation.

The client, a self-professed liberal in her 40s who works in the entertainment industry in the Los Angeles area, was relieved to see the new portfolio of investments wasn't invested in guns or prison-related companies. But she knew she had to make changes to the portfolio.

"She has some very strongly held values and a vision for her investments," Soelter said. Her newly inherited portfolio didn't align with that, and so she divested.

It's a tale as old as time: A child holds different values than the parents who have passed along wealth. And younger generations are grappling with inheriting record wealth right now.

A third of wealthy families in North America are in the process of transferring wealth, according to a report from UBS Global Wealth Management published earlier this year. UBS estimates that over the next two to three decades, roughly $83 trillion in private wealth will change hands, marking the largest wealth transfer in recent history, while Cerulli puts the figure at closer to $124 trillion by 2048.

At the same time, studies have shown that younger generations are more likely to invest in companies that align with their values, giving financial advisors the task of helping younger generations sell inherited assets and buy ones that more closely align with their goals, as Soelter recently did.

Younger generations have also come of age alongside technological advancements for the financial markets including the invention of low-cost index exchange-traded funds (ETFs) that give investors exposure to a range of securities with just one purchase.

James Mayo, a Denver-based advisor is currently helping a client in her late 30s who works in the legal industry transition over half a million dollars she had inherited in various high-fee active mutual funds.

There was a lot of overlap between the funds and no real strategy or plan linked to them, Mayo said. It is a common problem. Many of his clients with inherited assets come to him with high-cost actively managed funds that were purchased long before low-cost index funds became popular.

Technological innovation has also given investors the ability to be more choosy about what they put in their portfolio. With a few clicks on their phone, they can invest in cryptocurrency, and they are increasingly getting more access to private assets. At the same time, they are losing faith in the traditional stocks and bonds their parents and grandparents banked their retirement on.

Garrett Reeg, a St. Louis-based financial advisor with Moneta, recently worked with a middle-aged couple who had inherited an eight-figure portfolio of various investments, but who had a real interest in private investments. Reeg helped them get some exposure, including to private equity and venture capital, and build out a disciplined annual pacing approach aimed at improving their diversification and the overall return profile, while staying aligned with what they needed in terms of liquidity.

"Private investments have been very popular and access to them is increasing, so they viewed it as a way to enhance the return profile and risk associated with the portfolio," Reeg said. "Companies are staying private for longer...and there's a lot of value creation in the private markets that you don't have access to as a pure public investor. They wanted those opportunities as a piece of the portfolio given they could stomach the illiquidity aspect."

There's a lot more than just preference that goes into making changes to an inherited portfolio. Timing, liquidity and how investments fit into your overall portfolio are also important considerations. But the key consideration is usually taxes, and sometimes it can even overshadow a beneficiary's desire to invest in companies that better align with their values or to invest in more exciting assets.

"If it's a taxable account and selling would trigger a meaningful tax bill, people are much more willing to delay realigning the portfolio to their values and prioritize tax planning instead," Mayo said. "That might mean selling gradually, setting a tax budget or simply waiting for a better opportunity to make changes."

Write to editors@barrons.com

This content was created by Barron's, which is operated by Dow Jones & Co. Barron's is published independently from Dow Jones Newswires and The Wall Street Journal.

data.title: India's Kotak Bank Q2 profit rises 29%, beats estimates
data.description:
By Gopika Gopakumar

India's Kotak Mahindra Bank reported a higher-than-expected quarterly profit on ​Saturday, driven by stronger loan demand and lower ‌provisions for bad loans.

The country’s third-largest private lender by market capitalisation posted a stand-alone net profit of 42.11 billion Indian ​rupees ($443.5 million) for the three months ended September, ​up from 32.53 billion rupees for the same period last year.

Analysts had ⁠expected a profit of 41.04 billion rupees, according to ​data compiled by LSEG.

Indian banks experienced strong loan growth during the financial second quarter ​across both corporate and retail segments, with lending against foreign-currency non-resident deposits ‌also ⁠contributing to growth.

In June, the Reserve Bank of India introduced measures, including concessional hedging facilities and swap arrangements, to attract foreign currency deposits.

Kotak Bank's net interest income rose 16% to 84.6 ⁠billion rupees, aided by a 25% rise in domestic loans. Deposits grew 23%.

Its net interest margin, a key measure of the bank's profitability, fell to 4.31% from 4.53% three months earlier on account of FCNR deposit mobilisation during the quarter.

Funds ​kept aside ⁠for potential bad loans and other losses fell 15% to 8.04 billion rupees.

The bank's other ​income, which includes income from bonds and ​other investments, ⁠rose 23% year on year to 31.94 billion rupees amid volatile currency and debt markets.

The Mumbai-based lender's asset quality improved marginally, with the gross non-performing asset ⁠ratio ​at 1.04% at the end ​of September, compared with 1.18% in the prior three months.

($1 = 94.9400 Indian rupees)

data.title: Kotak Mahindra Bank Q2 results: Net profit jumps 29.5%, NII rises nearly 16%
data.description:
Kotak Mahindra Bank reported a 29.5% year-on-year jump in net profit to ₹4,212 crore in the September quarter of FY27, up from ₹3,253.3 crore a year earlier, according to an exchange filing.

Net interest income, the difference between interest earned and interest paid, rose 15.7% to ₹8,459 crore from ₹7,311 crore. Operating profit increased 21.1% year-on-year to ₹6,382.2 crore, compared with ₹5,268.3 crore in the year-ago quarter.

Net interest margin (NIM), a key measure of lending profitability, declined to 4.31% in the September quarter from 4.54% a year earlier and 4.53% in the June quarter.

Asset quality improves; provisions decline year-on-year

Kotak Mahindra Bank's asset quality improved sequentially during the quarter. Gross non-performing assets (GNPA) for the September quarter declined to 1.04% from 1.18% in the June quarter. Net non-performing assets (NNPA) fell to 0.24% from 0.27% over the same period.

Provisions stood at ₹803.6 crore, down 15.2% from ₹947.4 crore in the year-ago quarter. However, provisions increased 20.3% quarter-on-quarter from ₹668 crore in the June quarter, as per exchange filing.

Net advances rise 25%; FCNR(B) deposits boost funding base

Net advances increased 25% year-on-year to ₹5,77,295 crore as of September 30, 2026, from ₹4,62,688 crore a year earlier. Excluding loans extended against FCNR(B) deposits and the loan portfolio acquired from Kotak Mahindra Investments Ltd (KMIL), net advances grew 19% year-on-year.

The bank mobilised FCNR(B) deposits worth ₹55,344 crore during the September quarter through its international branches.

Kotak Mahindra Bank's current account and savings account (CASA) ratio stood at 38.2% as of September 30, 2026, compared with 42.3% a year earlier. The bank attributed the decline to an increase in the term deposit base following FCNR(B) deposit inflows. Excluding FCNR(B) deposits, the CASA ratio stood at 41.8%, according to exchange filing.

Shares of Kotak Mahindra Bank ended 1.5% lower at ₹430.50 on the NSE on Friday, October 23. The stock has gained 4.2% over the past month but remains down 2.9% so far this year.

data.title: Indonesia cuts pipeline gas exports to Singapore by about 9%
data.description:
Indonesia cut 31 million standard cubic feet gas per day (mmscfd) from its pipeline natural gas exports to Singapore starting on Saturday to divert supply to the domestic power sector, upstream oil and gas regulator SKK Migas said.

  • Indonesia cut 15 mmscfd from its supply to Singapore from Natuna and another 16 mmscfd gas from Sumatra, SKK Migas chairman Djoko Siswanto told Reuters on Saturday

  • Most of Indonesia’s gas exports to Singapore are delivered via pipeline, and the cuts would account for around 9% of that supply

  • “In order to safeguard the reliability of domestic gas supplies for electricity generation, effective today, gas supplies previously destined for Singapore are being redirected for domestic use,” said Djoko

  • The gas is being redirected to meet electricity needs in Batam, Bintan and Sumatra, he said

  • Batam and several cities in Indonesia’s Riau Islands province suffered a blackout that lasted 16 hours earlier this month

  • Indonesia energy minister Bahlil Lahadalia earlier this week said he would prioritise natural resources use for domestic needs, and review contracts to maintain energy security

  • Singapore generates up to ⁠95% of its electricity from natural gas

data.title: Trump, Biden Reportedly Asked SpaceX To Toggle SpaceX’s Starlink Services In Ukraine, Middle East — 'Elon Will Never Do Anything Wrong,' Says President
data.description:
Key points:
  • Officials in the two administrations shared intelligence with SpaceX indicating that the groups had obtained diverted Starlink terminals through intermediaries.
  • The Biden administration also pushed SpaceX to expand Starlink access for Ukraine after Russia's invasion in 2022.
  • The Trump administration reportedly made similar requests following U.S.-Israeli strikes on Iran in 2025 and 2026.

Space Exploration Technologies Corp. (SPCX) has reportedly been asked multiple times by the Biden and Trump administrations to toggle its Starlink services in Ukraine and the Middle East.

According to a Reuters report citing sources familiar with the matter, the requests by both administrations included expanding the availability of Starlink services in Ukraine and Iran, while restricting access to Iran-backed groups in the Middle East.

SpaceX shares gained nearly 2% in Friday’s regular trading session, and edged up by 0.1% further during the afterhours trade.

US Asked Musk To Control Starlink Access, Says Report

According to the report, officials in the two administrations shared intelligence with SpaceX indicating that the groups had obtained diverted Starlink terminals through intermediaries.

The terminals were subsequently deactivated in some cases, the report noted. The Biden administration also pushed SpaceX to expand Starlink access for Ukraine after Russia's invasion in 2022.

The Biden administration separately asked SpaceX to activate Starlink in Iran during protests in the country, with the U.S. government helping move Starlink terminals into Iran.

The Trump administration reportedly made similar requests following U.S.-Israeli strikes on Iran in 2025 and 2026. Trump officials discussed with Musk and SpaceX getting Starlink terminals into Iran and activating them to improve internet access and communications for anti-government protesters.

Starlink Under Scrutiny Over Slowdown Concerns In Ukraine

This comes amid concerns that SpaceX’s Starlink services have been slowed down in Ukraine.

Last week, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said the restrictions had affected military drones, while reports suggested that the order to throttle Starshield came from inside the White House.

SpaceX CEO Elon Musk has maintained that SpaceX-powered Starshield systems are owned and controlled by the U.S. government and that decisions on speed or usage ultimately rest with the U.S. military and the president.

Trump Backs Musk

Amid this, Trump told reporters on Friday that while he believes that the Starlink throttling issue over Ukraine has been fixed, he would speak to Musk if that is not the case. He also backed the SpaceX CEO, saying that he’s a “good person.”

“He’s not going to do anything wrong. He’s a very brilliant person, or Starlink wouldn’t exist. But Elon will never do anything wrong, I know him very well. He’s a fair person,” Trump said.

What Retail Investors Think Of SPCX Stock

Retail sentiment on Stocktwits around SpaceX trended in the ‘extremely bullish’ territory at the time of writing.

One bullish user believes that SpaceX is a “no brainer” for investment, highlighting the company’s “cutting edge technology” on offer.

View this Stocktwits post

SPCX stock is down 2% year-to-date. The S&P 500 ETF (SPY) is up 11% over the past 12 months, while the Vanguard Morningstar Total Stock Market ETF (VTI) is up 10%.

data.title: Invest In Infra, Registrations And Test Facilities Before Expecting Any Order: SRL's CMD
data.description:
Shree Refrigerations’ R.G. Shende says mission-critical indigenisation demands years of demonstrated performance on board naval vessels, steady servicing and a willingness to build Navy feedback into product upgrades

India’s defence indigenisation push has moved from policy to practice, but the real test lies in the small and mid-sized firms that supply the “invisible” subsystems inside large platforms. R.G. Shende, Chairman and Managing Director of Shree Refrigerations Limited (SRL), says his company developed air conditioning for Scorpene submarines without foreign collaboration. In this interview, he explains what it takes to earn the Indian Navy’s trust, why infrastructure and test facilities must come before orders, and why policy should reserve MSME benefits for companies with at least 51 per cent local ownership.

India has set ambitious goals for defence indigenisation and exports, backed by positive indigenous lists and rising capital budgets. How far has the country come in building real domestic capability, as opposed to assembling imported systems, and where is the gap still widest?

For a country that builds rockets and all the high-tech equipment, defence indigenisation comes naturally and without much technological challenge. All it needed was governmental buying and support for indigenisation by way of negative lists and mandatory local content. Although some equipment needs to be imported due to economic considerations, most manufacturing and integration can be local, cutting dependence on foreign tech.

The government also supports tech development through the indigenisation push in schemes such as iDEX (Innovations for Defence Excellence) and ADITI (Acing Development of Innovative Technologies with iDEX). Tech support is also available from DRDO by way of Transfer of Technology (ToT) to private enterprises. Patient capital is also made available for innovation funding. The results are there to be seen. In our own case, we were able to develop ACs for Scorpene submarines without any foreign collaboration.

Large defence platforms are built on the work of hundreds of specialised suppliers, many of them small and mid-sized, in areas such as cooling, controls and fabrication. Why do these “invisible” subsystems matter so much to a platform’s performance, and are they getting the attention and support they deserve?

Definitely. Dependence on foreign vendors needs to be reduced to a minimum to avoid a big drain on forex outflow. Quality control by the Director General of Quality Control (DGQA) ensures that the equipment is up to the exacting standards of workmanship and quality. All this happens at a fraction of the cost of imported equipment and service. Besides, post-installation service is also available locally and is highly price competitive.

Replacing an imported subsystem with an Indian-made one demands engineering depth, testing and years of trust-building with the Indian Navy. What does it actually take to indigenise a mission-critical system, and what do people outside the industry underestimate?

Perseverance, patience and focus are needed to demonstrate a firm’s commitment to serving the Navy. The firm has to establish credentials that take years to build and moments to lose. That is where the promoter’s (and his team’s) integrity and firm commitment matter. This is not for the faint-hearted. The ability to develop tech, demonstrate it on board naval vessels over a longer duration, service it over the years, and integrate Naval feedback into product upgrades are the important aspects.

Naval platforms need cooling and climate control that works in extreme heat, humidity, vibration and confined spaces, while energy efficiency and reliability are rising priorities. Which technologies will shape the next generation of marine and defence HVAC, and how ready is India to build them at home?

The focus here is more on stealth, reliability and serviceability. All the tech is available within India. Firms only have to rise to the occasion, bring out their best and deliver.

You spent over two decades in commercial refrigeration and air conditioning before turning towards defence. What did you have to unlearn, build or invest in to make that shift, and what advice would you give mid-sized industrial companies considering the same path?

Have heart, believe in yourself, ensure deep pockets and go for it. More importantly, invest in infra, registrations and a test facility before expecting any order. These are prerequisites and not something to be done “after I get the order”. The advantage here is long-term visibility of business, which allows you to build capacity and capability ahead of the market opportunity.

Defence manufacturing involves long approval cycles, rigorous qualification and large working-capital needs, and public markets are now showing strong interest in the sector. How should mid-sized defence suppliers balance patient, long-gestation growth with the expectations of investors?

Efficiency. That’s it. Invest in modernisation, better project execution capability, lower cash cycles and a strong order book. If the forces have faith in you, investors will.

India’s defence ecosystem is opening up to private players of all sizes, yet procurement processes remain demanding and slow for newcomers. What reforms would do the most to bring more capable private manufacturers into the supply chain and keep them there?

The government has done enough. It is time for Indian industry to rise to the occasion and demonstrate its skills and commitment. There is some scope for improvement in expediting payments, especially to MSMEs; this, over and above the TReDS channel, will help. The anomaly is that large foreign OEMs open a small office in India, harvest the local supply chains, become MSMEs in India and enjoy all the benefits of a local MSME. These firms have access to large overseas funds and can easily leverage their foreign clout to outbid a local MSME. The challenge is that the equipment still has foreign IP. This is not in line with Aatmanirbhar Bharat, although it may qualify under the Make in India norms of x per cent local content. This defeats the spirit of Aatmanirbhar Bharat. Policymakers need to review the policy to ensure that the benefits are available to companies with a minimum of 51 per cent local ownership. This will ensure higher participation of Indian MSMEs in this national capability-building initiative.

Looking ahead 10 years, what would a self-reliant Indian defence supply chain look like, in terms of exports, technology ownership and the role of small and mid-sized companies, and what has to happen to get there?

Companies requiring after-sales service support will find it challenging to export to foreign nations. The business volume needs to justify creating a service infrastructure in the customer country. Also, most countries would like to emulate their own version of “Make in My Country”. Exports are possible by way of JVs with local companies. Again, companies need to create that level of credibility. They also need to exhibit at foreign expos and trade shows, and demonstrate their capability, reference list, infrastructure and service capability at short notice. Again, build credibility and trust. This is a long process and there are no shortcuts.

Savi Khanna

BW Reporters Assistant Editor, BW Businessworld

data.title: Lemon Tree Hotels signs Keys Lite property in Bhilwara
data.description:
Lemon Tree Hotels Limited has signed Keys Lite by Lemon Tree Hotels, Bhilwara, strengthening its presence in Rajasthan. The property will be managed by Carnation Hotels Private Limited, a wholly owned subsidiary of Lemon Tree Hotels Limited.

Located in Bhilwara, a commercial centre known for its textile industry and business activity, the hotel will cater to business and leisure travellers. The property will feature 63 rooms, a restaurant, banquet facilities, a meeting/conference room, a fitness centre and other public areas.

Vishvapreet Singh Cheema, president, Lemon Tree Hotels Limited, said, "Rajasthan continues to be an important growth market for us, defined by a strong mix of commercial dynamism and rich tourism. Bhilwara, a key textile and industrial centre, presents a natural opportunity for Keys Lite to cater to the rising demand for reliable, value-driven hospitality. This signing scales our footprint to 24 hotels in the state and underscores our focused approach to expanding across India’s key industrial hubs and emerging secondary markets."

Bhilwara Railway Station is approximately 1.5 km from the property, while Maharana Pratap Airport in Udaipur is approximately 148 km away. With this signing, Lemon Tree Hotels will have 14 operational and 10 upcoming hotels in Rajasthan.

data.title: BPCL Q2 Profit Falls 21% To Rs 4,863 Cr As Margins Weigh
data.description:
Higher revenue from operations was offset by lower marketing margins on certain petroleum products, while first-half profit fell sharply

Bharat Petroleum Corporation (BPCL) reported a 21.4 per cent year-on-year decline in consolidated net profit to Rs 4,863.05 crore for the July-September quarter of FY27, compared with Rs 6,191.49 crore in the corresponding period last year.

Revenue from operations rose 29.8 per cent to Rs 1.58 lakh crore from Rs 1.22 lakh crore a year earlier. Total expenses increased to Rs 1.52 lakh crore from Rs 1.15 lakh crore, while profit before tax, including the share of profit from equity-accounted investees and exceptional items, declined to Rs 6,559.80 crore from Rs 8,344.59 crore.

The company’s standalone results showed a similar trend, with net profit falling 22.5 per cent year on year to Rs 4,993.17 crore from Rs 6,442.53 crore. Standalone revenue from operations increased to Rs 1.58 lakh crore from Rs 1.22 lakh crore.

For the first half of FY27, BPCL’s consolidated net profit declined to Rs 2,990.35 crore from Rs 13,030.51 crore in the corresponding period last year. Consolidated revenue from operations rose to Rs 3.17 lakh crore from Rs 2.51 lakh crore.

Marketing Margins Weigh

BPCL said lower profit during April-September 2026 was mainly due to suppressed marketing margins on certain petroleum products, partly offset by higher refining margins.

The company also reported a cumulative net negative buffer of Rs 17,334.40 crore in its liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) account as of 30 September 2026, up from Rs 12,318.52 crore at the end of March. Revenue from LPG sales has not been recognised to the extent of this negative buffer.

The Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas had approved compensation of Rs 7,594 crore towards under-recoveries on domestic LPG sales incurred up to March 2025 and expected up to March 2026. BPCL recognised six monthly installments aggregating Rs 3,796.98 crore during the first half of FY27.

BPCL’s refinery throughput increased to 10.41 million tonne in the September quarter from 9.82 million tonne a year earlier. Domestic market sales rose to 13.47 million tonne from 12.67 million tonne, while export sales increased to 0.59 million tonne from 0.36 million tonne.

data.title: Lava International Faces Leadership Shake-Up Amid Rs 600 Cr Fundraise Plans
data.description:
The handset maker is targeting the sub-Rs 20,000 smartphone segment while reportedly exploring a Rs 500–600 crore fundraise

Lava International Managing Director Sunil Raina and Chief Financial Officer Rajesh Sethi are set to step down from their respective roles by December, as the Indian smartphone maker looks to secure fresh capital and revive business growth. Co-founder Hari Om Rai, who stepped down as managing director in 2023, has returned to the role.

A company spokesperson confirmed the departures, saying that Raina and Sethi had decided to move on from their positions. Sethi was acknowledged for his contributions to the company’s financial operations and business priorities.

Leadership Changes At Lava

According to reports, both executives have submitted their resignations and are serving their notice periods, with their exits expected by December. Raina is reportedly leaving to pursue business ventures outside Lava.Raina joined Lava in 2010 as Vice-President and Chief Marketing Officer before moving through several senior positions. He took over as interim managing director in November 2023 after Rai was arrested by the Enforcement Directorate in a money-laundering case linked to Vivo. Raina was formally elevated to managing director in June 2025.

Sethi joined Lava as Group Chief Financial Officer in May 2024. Before joining the handset maker, he worked with Iraq-based Ster Group and held positions at Bharti Airtel, Telenor Group and Essar Group.The latest departures follow the exit of Sanjeev Agarwal, who served as Chief Manufacturing Officer and later as Executive Director and Chief Manufacturing Officer at Lava.

Focus On Affordable Smartphones

The leadership changes come as Lava seeks to strengthen its position in the smartphone segment priced below Rs 20,000. The company has previously said its smartphone business grew by 60–70 per cent during the year, despite a contraction in the overall market.The sub-Rs 20,000 segment represents an opportunity for the company as it seeks to revive growth and expand its market presence.

Fundraising And Stake Sale Talks

Lava is also reportedly exploring a fundraise of around Rs 500–600 crore to finance expansion and potentially restructure part of its debt.Earlier reports have suggested that promoters of electronics manufacturers Dixon Technologies and Amber Enterprises are in discussions to acquire stakes in Lava in their personal capacities. The reported discussions and fundraising plans come as the company navigates leadership changes and seeks fresh capital to support its next phase of growth.

data.title: Tech Mahindra Acquires Finastra’s Cash Management Suite
data.description:
The deal adds cash management, virtual accounts and liquidity management products to Tech Mahindra’s banking technology portfolio

Tech Mahindra has acquired the cash management product suite of Finastra, comprising Fusion Cash Management, Fusion Virtual Accounts and Fusion Liquidity Management, expanding its portfolio of banking technology solutions. The financial details of the transaction have not been disclosed.

The acquisition is aimed at supporting continued product investment, innovation and business growth within Tech Mahindra’s Banking, Financial Services and Insurance (BFSI) business. It also provides for continuity of services and support for existing customers while bringing product engineering and customer success professionals into Tech Mahindra.

Expanding Banking Solutions

The acquired portfolio includes three products covering cash management, virtual accounts and liquidity management. These solutions form part of the technology infrastructure used by financial institutions to manage corporate banking and treasury-related requirements.

The addition broadens Tech Mahindra’s banking solutions portfolio as it continues to develop its offerings for the financial services sector.

Focus On Product Development

Tech Mahindra intends to continue investing in the acquired products, with a focus on innovation and growth within its BFSI business. The transaction also brings experienced product engineering talent into the company, supporting the ongoing development and management of the suite.

Customer success professionals are also part of the talent transition, helping maintain support for organisations already using the products.

Customer Service Continuity

The acquisition includes provisions for continued services and support for existing customers. This is intended to maintain operational continuity as the products and associated teams transition to Tech Mahindra.

The financial terms of the deal and further details about the integration process have not been disclosed.

The transaction adds to Tech Mahindra’s banking technology capabilities through an established suite of cash and liquidity management products, while placing continued product investment and customer support among the stated priorities of the acquisition.

data.title: STL Appoints Lakshmi Iyer To Lead M&A & Capital Market Strategy
data.description:
The corporate development executive joins from Tata Power, where she worked on strategic capital allocation exceeding USD 3 billion

Sterlite Technologies (STL) has appointed Lakshmi Iyer as Chief – Mergers and Acquisitions (M&A), Investor Relations and Capital Markets Strategy, effective October 2026. Iyer joins the optical connectivity solutions provider after nearly three years at Tata Power, where she served as Head – Strategic Finance and M&A, working on capital allocation across energy-transition initiatives.

In her new role, Iyer will focus on mergers and acquisitions, strategic partnerships, investor relations and capital markets strategy as STL looks to pursue growth opportunities in optical connectivity. The appointment comes amid rising demand for connectivity infrastructure, driven in part by the expansion of artificial intelligence-led data centres.

Experience Across Capital Allocation

At Tata Power, Iyer worked on strategic capital allocation exceeding USD 3 billion across energy-transition initiatives. Her responsibilities included supporting investments intended to contribute to the energy sector’s transition.

She held the position of Head – Strategic Finance and M&A from January 2024 to September 2026. Before joining Tata Power, she had also worked at STL from May 2021 to December 2023 as Head – Mergers and Acquisitions and Investor Relations.

Extensive Deal Experience

Iyer brings around 25 years of experience in corporate development and investments, with a focus on cross-border M&A, capital raising and take-private transactions. Her experience spans energy, core infrastructure, industrials and technology across Asia-Pacific, Africa, North America, Europe and the Middle East.

She previously spent more than four years at GMR Group as Head – Mergers, Divestments and Acquisitions, followed by over eight years at Essar in a senior M&A and capital-raising role.

Her work has included buy-side and sell-side transactions, debt and equity fundraising, and complex deals involving multiple markets and regulatory frameworks. Her cumulative deal experience exceeds USD 15 billion, according to her professional profile.

Focus On Optical Connectivity

At STL, Iyer will work across M&A, investor relations and capital markets strategy. The company operates in optical connectivity, a segment facing increasing infrastructure requirements as AI-led data centres expand.

Her return to STL follows her earlier tenure at the company in an M&A and investor relations leadership role. The combination of her previous experience at STL and her more recent work in energy-sector investments at Tata Power brings together exposure to technology infrastructure, strategic finance and capital allocation.

Iyer holds a Master of Business Administration from SDA Bocconi and has completed an executive programme in general management and leadership at Columbia Business School.

data.title: KEC International Bags Rs 2,872 Cr Power Grid Orders For kV765 Lines
data.description:
The contracts will support the evacuation of 8.5 GW of renewable energy from Gujarat, taking KEC International’s FY27 year-to-date order intake beyond Rs 13,500 crore

KEC International has secured orders worth Rs 2,872 crore from Power Grid Corporation of India (PGCIL) for the design, supply and installation of 765 kV transmission lines. The projects will facilitate the evacuation of 8.5 gigawatts (GW) of renewable energy from Gujarat, according to a regulatory filing dated 24 October.

The company said the contracts represent the largest-ever single order for its India transmission and distribution (T&D) business, significantly expanding its domestic order book.

Vimal Kejriwal, Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of KEC International, said the latest contracts reflected continued momentum in the company's T&D business. "These prestigious 765 kV projects, associated with the evacuation of 8.5 GW of renewable energy from Gujarat, have substantially expanded our India T&D order book," Kejriwal said.

The company remains confident about the growth prospects of India's T&D sector, supported by rising energy demand and the country's continued focus on strengthening transmission infrastructure. With the latest wins, KEC International's cumulative order intake for the current financial year to date has crossed Rs 13,500 crore. The T&D business accounts for around Rs 9,500 crore of this total, the company said.

Headquartered in Mumbai, KEC International is the flagship infrastructure engineering, procurement and construction company of RPG Group. Its business portfolio includes power transmission and distribution, civil construction, transportation, renewable energy, oil and gas pipelines, and cables and conductors.

KEC International shares closed around 1.5 per cent lower at Rs 327 apiece on the National Stock Exchange on 23 October. The stock has declined nearly 56 per cent so far in 2026.

data.title: India's emerging sectors to drive capex, credit demand towards storage, semiconductors: Report
data.description:
New Delhi, Oct. 24 -- Financing demand in India's emerging sectors is expected to shift towards battery storage, semiconductor packaging, green hydrogen projects with assured buyers and defence suppliers over the next three to five years, as investments in new growth industries create opportunities for banks, according to a Union Bank of India research report.

The report noted artificial intelligence (AI), semiconductors and defence is likely to lead the investment pipeline, with indicative public and private investments of around Rs 5.9 lakh crore, Rs 5.27 lakh crore and Rs 5.07 lakh crore, respectively.

It said financing opportunities would increasingly emerge in advanced packaging and assembly of semiconductors, battery recycling, lithium iron phosphate (LFP) and sodium-ion battery capacity, storage infrastructure and component suppliers to the defence industry.

The report also highlighted the potential for financing hydrogen projects backed by assured offtake agreements, while demand for data centres is expected to expand towards edge and colocation facilities as AI inference grows.

However, the report cautioned that technology obsolescence, uncertain revenues, delayed payments and long investment payback periods remain significant risks for lenders.

Semiconductor projects typically have payback periods of five to eight years, while space projects may take seven to ten years, exceeding conventional loan tenures, it said. AI infrastructure also faces rapid technology cycles, with graphics processing unit clusters requiring upgrades every 18 to 24 months.

The report said ten of the twelve emerging sectors already had identifiable debt-financing routes, while AI and space remained predominantly equity-funded due to technology risks and long payback periods.

It recommended that banks develop specialised lending capabilities for semiconductors, hydrogen, data centres and battery storage, alongside products such as milestone-linked disbursements, receivables financing, equipment leasing and green loans.

The report identified renewable energy, semiconductors, green hydrogen and critical minerals as sectors suited to project finance and development finance institution-led funding, while electric vehicles and drones could benefit from asset financing and non-banking financial company lending.

India's renewable energy capacity stood at 288.6 GW against a target of 500 GW by 2030, while the electric vehicle and battery storage market was projected to grow from USD 34 billion to USD 113 billion by 2030.

The report said financing opportunities would increasingly move towards commercially viable projects and supply-chain participants as these emerging sectors expand.

data.title: Compass Therapeutics, Inc. (CMPX) Posts Positive Phase 2/3 BTC Results
data.description:
Key points:
  • As published in the Journal of Clinical Oncology (JCO) and presented at ESMO, COMPANION-002 met its primary endpoint of ORR and key secondary endpoint of PFS, with a 56% reduction in the risk of disease progression or death.
  • Responses were durable, with a median duration of response (DOR) of 4.9 months, and disease control rate (DCR) was also significantly improved (62.2% vs. 36.8%).
  • A new, post hoc analysis of overall survival (OS) included in the JCO publication uses the Two-Stage Estimation, an established method for adjusting for crossover, and demonstrates an OS hazard ratio of 0.85 (95% CI, 0.59–1.26; p=0.53).
  • Safety profile was consistent with prior tovecimig studies and the anti-VEGF class, with no new safety signals identified.

Compass Therapeutics published Phase 2/3 data showing tovecimig plus paclitaxel improved ORR to 18.0% vs 5.3% and median PFS to 4.7 vs 2.6 months (HR=0.44) in previously treated advanced biliary tract cancer.

Material Details

#DetailAI Analyst View
1ORR 18.0% vs 5.3% (p=0.0228)Signals added activity over chemo in 2L BTC, a high-need setting.
2Median PFS 4.7 vs 2.6 mo (HR=0.44)56% lower risk of progression/death supports clinical benefit.
3Peer-reviewed in JCO; ESMO 2026 talkValidation and visibility can influence regulator and investor views.
4168 pts; randomized 2:1 designControlled dataset lends credibility to efficacy signals.
5Fast Track & Orphan US FDA statusMay expedite development and review timelines.
6Activity post-crossover notedHints at drug effect even after progression on control.

Context by AI Analyst

This is a mid-stage clinical validation step for CMPX’s lead bispecific in a niche oncology setting with no approved 2L standard. A larger catalyst would be FDA alignment on a registrational path or filing plans supported by OS analyses and safety data.

6Grade 3 stomatitis <3% by cycle 2Manageable toxicity reduces risk of treatment interruptions.

This is a follow-on readout from VIKTORIA-1 after FDA approval for a related setting, reinforcing efficacy and tolerability signals. For a larger catalyst, full dataset updates, regulatory label expansions, or guideline inclusion would need to follow.

data.title: Johnson & Johnson's prostate cancer drug shrinks tumors in early-stage trial
data.description:
Johnson & Johnson on Saturday said its experimental once-daily oral prostate cancer drug caused tumors to disappear or shrink in an early-stage trial.

J&J had gained access to the drug through its $3.05 billion deal to buy Halda Therapeutics last year.

Here are more details:

  • The company was testing JNJ-6143 in patients with advanced prostate cancer who had received multiple treatments

  • Its novel approach selectively kills cancer cells by interfering with a protein they need to survive

  • In the trial, 77% of 31 evaluable patients receiving the 50-milligram dose saw their PSA levels, a blood marker used to monitor prostate cancer, fall by at least 50%; in 48% of patients, PSA levels fell by at least 90%

  • Among patients whose tumors could be measured using imaging, 69% had a confirmed complete or partial response

  • "It adds a new mechanism of action to J&J's prostate cancer portfolio," a Johnson & Johnson spokesperson said

  • Common side effects were nausea and elevated cholesterol and triglyceride levels. One patient discontinued treatment due to adverse effects

  • The data were presented at the European Society for Medical Oncology Congress
